plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Entire avenues disappear under clouds of trumpet-shaped, lavender-blue blossoms. The petals carpet pavements and parked cars in violet drifts beneath feathery, fern-like foliage.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring, peaking in October in the southern hemisphere
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, which is nicknamed the Jacaranda City, and other southern-hemisphere cities such as Buenos Aires
plants.funFact: Native to South America, the jacaranda was planted so widely in Pretoria that the city's whole skyline turns purple every October.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Airy, daisy-like blooms float on slender stems above delicate, threadlike foliage. They sway in the autumn breeze and draw butterflies and bees to the late-season garden.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through autumn, roughly June to October in temperate gardens
plants.location: Temperate gardens of the northern hemisphere, such as the US Midwest; native to Mexico
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek word kosmos, meaning order or harmony, a nod to the tidy symmetry of its petals.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: Tall, sturdy stems end in clusters of starry, purple-rayed flowers with golden centers. They light up meadows and roadsides just as the autumn foliage turns, and they are a favorite stop for migrating monarch butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn, about August through October
plants.location: Meadows and prairies of eastern and central North America, including Maryland and Missouri
plants.funFact: Its flowers are among the last big nectar sources of the year, so they help fuel migrating butterflies on their long journey south.
